## Design notes

**Envelope**
- `id` — unique per event. Use it as the idempotency key so consumers can safely discard duplicates (deliveries are typically at-least-once).
- `type` — a stable, namespaced event name (`subscription.renewed`). Use past tense to describe what happened.
- `api_version` — version the schema so you can evolve fields without breaking consumers. Add new optional fields rather than removing or retyping existing ones.
- `occurred_at` — when the renewal happened (UTC, ISO 8601), distinct from when the webhook was delivered.
- `livemode` — lets consumers ignore sandbox/test events.

**`data`**
- Nest related objects (`subscription`, `customer`, `plan`, `billing`) rather than flattening everything into one level — easier to read and to evolve.
- Amounts as **integer minor units** (5292 = $52.92) plus an explicit ISO 4217 `currency`; never use floats.
- Include both `current_period_start`/`current_period_end` and `next_billing_date` so consumers can reconcile periods without calling back.
- `metadata` carries your own identifiers (account, workspace) so the receiver doesn't need a lookup.
- Keep sensitive data out: no full card numbers, no raw tax IDs, no secrets. Reference objects by ID instead.

**Delivery**
- Sign the raw request body with an HMAC-SHA256 secret and send it in a header, e.g. `Webhook-Signature: t=1730451272,v1=<hex_digest>`. Verify the timestamp to prevent replay.
- Retry with exponential backoff on non-2xx responses; expect duplicates and out-of-order delivery, so consumers should be idempotent and reconcile state rather than trust sequence.
- Respond `2xx` quickly; do slow work asynchronously.
- Include a `Webhook-Id`/`X-Request-Id` header for tracing.

**Optional additions**
- `data.billing.proration` — populated when a renewal is adjusted mid-cycle (amount, period, reason).
- `data.billing.discount` and `data.billing.tax` — `null` when not applicable.
- `data.subscription.renewal_count` — useful for loyalty/usage-based logic.
- A `changes` object (e.g. `{"quantity": {"from": 2, "to": 3}}`) if the renewal also modified the subscription — otherwise emit a separate `subscription.updated` event.

# Subscription Renewal Webhook — Payload Design

## 1. Design principles

| Principle | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **Envelope + typed `data.object`** | One receiver can route on `type` without parsing the body; new event types don't break existing handlers. |
| **Snapshot, not a pointer** | The body reflects state *at renewal time*. Don't make consumers call back to your API for every field. |
| **Money as integer minor units** | `4900` + `"currency": "usd"`. Never floats, never `"$49.00"`. |
| **UTC ISO-8601 timestamps** | `2024-09-01T12:00:03Z`. One format everywhere. |
| **Stable `id` across retries** | The single idempotency key. Redeliveries reuse the same `id`. |
| **Explicit `null`s** | Distinguish "no proration" from "field omitted" — matters when you add fields later. |
| **No raw PAN / no PII bloat** | PCI scope + data-minimization. Card data is a brand/last4 summary only. |

---

## 2. Event catalog

Emit these under the same envelope so one endpoint can serve them all:

| `type` | Emitted when |
|---|---|
| `subscription.renewed` | Billing cycle completed and payment succeeded. **The core event.** |
| `subscription.renewal_failed` | Auto-renewal charge failed (card declined, insufficient funds). |
| `subscription.trial_converted` | A trial rolled into its first paid period. |
| `subscription.canceled` | Renewal was skipped because the subscription was canceled at period end. |
| `subscription.paused` / `subscription.resumed` | Billing paused or resumed mid-cycle. |

---

## 3. The payload

```json
      "currency": "usd",
      "renewal_number": 12,
      "billing_cycle_anchor": "2023-10-01T00:00:00Z",
      "current_period_start": "2024-09-01T00:00:00Z",
      "current_period_end": "2024-10-01T00:00:00Z",
      "previous_period_end": "2024-09-01T00:00:00Z",
      "trial_end": null,
      "cancel_at_period_end": false,
      "canceled_at": null,

        "workspace_id": "ws_5512",
        "seats": "3"
      }
    },
    "invoice": {
      "id": "in_1Qa7bC2d",
      "number": "A-000123",
```

### Field notes

- **`renewal_number`** — monotonically increasing count of successful renewals on this subscription. Together with `data.object.id` it's the natural **business key** (`sub_8f3a91c2` + `12`) if you need to dedupe on the underlying transaction rather than the delivery.
- **`previous_attributes`** — only the fields that actually changed. Lets consumers react to a trial→active transition without diffing against their own copy. Omit the key entirely when nothing changed.
- **`proration`** — non-null only for mid-cycle plan changes or upgrades; include `credit_amount`, `charge_amount`, and `effective_at`.
- **`invoice.billing_reason`** — `subscription_cycle` for a normal renewal; `subscription_update` for a change-triggered invoice. Consumers often want to treat these differently.
- **`livemode: false`** — test-mode events. Consumers should filter these out of production ledgers.

---

## 4. HTTP delivery contract

```
POST /webhooks/billing
Content-Type: application/json
X-Webhook-Id: evt_01HQ8X2K9F3M7N
X-Webhook-Timestamp: 1725192003
X-Webhook-Signature: t=1725192003,v1=5257a869e7ec46b9c2b6f3a1d8e4c0b7a9f2e5d1c8b3a6f0e4d9c2b7a1e8f5d3
X-Webhook-Delivery-Attempt: 1
Idempotency-Key: evt_01HQ8X2K9F3M7N
```

**Signature verification** — HMAC-SHA256 over `"{timestamp}.{raw_body}"`, keyed with your endpoint secret, hex-encoded, constant-time compare. Reject if `|now - timestamp| > 300s` (replay protection). Always verify against the **raw** body bytes, before JSON parsing.

**Retries** — non-2xx or timeout (10s) triggers exponential backoff: ~1m, 5m, 30m, 2h, 6h, 12h, 24h (7 attempts over ~24h). The same `id` and `X-Webhook-Id` are reused on every attempt; only `X-Webhook-Delivery-Attempt` and `delivery_attempt` change.

**Ordering** — not guaranteed. Two renewals for the same subscription can arrive out of order under retry. Consumers should use `current_period_end` / `renewal_number` to detect and discard stale events, or re-fetch subscription state from the API when it matters.

**Idempotency** — store `id` for at least 7 days and drop duplicates. A renewal must never produce two downstream entitlements.

---

## 5. JSON Schema (abbreviated)

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://schemas.example.com/webhooks/subscription.renewed/2024-09-01",
  "title": "subscription.renewed",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id", "type", "api_version", "created_at", "livemode", "data"],
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "id": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^evt_[A-Za-z0-9]+$" },
    "type": { "const": "subscription.renewed" },
    "api_version": { "type": "string" },
    "created_at": { "type": "string", "format": "date-time" },
    "livemode": { "type": "boolean" },
    "delivery_attempt": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1 },
    "correlation_id": { "type": ["string", "null"] },
    "data": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["object", "invoice", "payment"],
      "properties": {
        "object": {
          "type": "object",
          "required": ["id", "object", "status", "customer", "plan",
                       "current_period_start", "current_period_end", "renewal_number"],
          "properties": {
            "id": { "type": "string" },
            "object": { "const": "subscription" },
            "status": {
              "enum": ["active", "trialing", "past_due", "paused", "canceled"]
            },
            "renewal_number": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 },
            "current_period_start": { "type": "string", "format": "date-time" },
            "current_period_end": { "type": "string", "format": "date-time" },
            "metadata": { "type": "object", "additionalProperties": { "type": "string" } }
          }
        },
        "invoice": {
          "type": "object",
          "required": ["id", "status", "total", "currency", "period_start", "period_end"],
          "properties": {
            "status": { "enum": ["draft", "open", "paid", "void", "uncollectible"] },
            "total": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 },
            "currency": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^[a-z]{3}$" }
          }
        },
        "payment": {
          "type": "object",
          "required": ["id", "status", "amount", "currency"],
          "properties": {
            "status": { "enum": ["succeeded", "failed", "pending"] },
            "method": {
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "type": { "enum": ["card", "sepa_debit", "ach", "paypal", "invoice"] },
                "brand": { "type": ["string", "null"] },
                "last4": { "type": ["string", "null"], "pattern": "^[0-9]{4}$" }
              }
            }
          }
        },
        "proration": { "type": ["object", "null"] },
        "discount": { "type": ["object", "null"] },
        "tax": { "type": ["object", "null"] }
      }
    },
    "previous_attributes": { "type": "object" }
  }
}
```

Publish this schema at a versioned URL and point the `api_version` field at it — consumers can validate offline and you get machine-checkable compatibility.

---

## 6. Versioning & evolution

- `api_version` is a **date** (`2024-09-01`). Within a version, only **additive** changes are allowed: new optional fields, new enum values in open-ended enums, new `type` strings.
- **Breaking** changes (renaming a field, changing units, removing a field, changing meaning) require a new `api_version`. Ship the new version alongside the old for a deprecation window, and let consumers pin a version via the endpoint URL (`/webhooks/billing/2024-09-01`) or a dashboard setting.
- Treat `status` and `method.type` enums as **open** — consumers must tolerate unknown values rather than erroring.

---

## 7. Security & operational checklist

- [ ] HMAC signature verified on the raw body, with timestamp tolerance and constant-time comparison.
- [ ] Endpoint secret rotatable without downtime (accept the previous secret for a grace period).
- [ ] No card numbers, no full bank details, no passwords in the payload — PCI scope stays narrow.
- [ ] `metadata` on the subscription passes through customer-supplied key/values; consider a size cap and a character whitelist so consumers aren't blindsided.
- [ ] Test-mode events carry `livemode: false` so they can't pollute production ledgers.
- [ ] Payload size kept under ~64 KB — if an invoice has many line items, include a summary plus a URL to the full invoice rather than inlining everything.
- [ ] A dead-letter queue after the final retry, with a replay tool that **reuses the original `id`** so consumers' idempotency checks still hold.
- [ ] Consumer-side dedupe on `id` (retention ≥ 7 days) *and* on `subscription.id` + `renewal_number` (business-level correctness).

```json
      "current_period_end": "2025-03-14T09:41:22Z",
      "status": "trialing"
    }
  },

  "request": {
    "id": "req_5Ab2",
    "idempotency_key": "sub_9Xk2LmQ7pR4t:2025-03-14"
  },

  "context": {
    "ip": "203.0.113.42",
    "user_agent": "Mozilla/5.0"
  }
}
```

## 2. Field reference

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `id` | Unique event ID. Use this as the idempotency key for dedupe. |
| `type` | Event name. `subscription.renewed` fires on successful billing of a new cycle. |
| `api_version` | Version of the payload schema, so consumers can branch safely. |
| `created_at` | When the event was generated (ISO 8601, UTC). |
| `livemode` | `false` for sandbox/test events — let consumers ignore them. |
| `delivery_attempt` | Increments on each retry attempt. |
| `data.object` | Full snapshot of the subscription *after* renewal (not a delta). |
| `data.renewal` | Renewal-specific summary: which cycle, amounts, tax, proration. |
| `data.invoice` | The invoice generated for this cycle, with line items and URLs. |
| `data.payment` | Outcome and method of the charge. `status: "failed"` is possible on a renewal attempt. |
| `data.previous_attributes` | Only the fields that changed vs. the prior state — useful for audit logs. |
| `data.object.metadata` | Your own metadata echoed back (order ID, workspace ID, etc.). |
| `request.idempotency_key` | Provider-side key for this billing operation; also good for your dedupe table. |

## 3. Minimal variant (if you want a lean payload)

```json
{
  "id": "evt_01HQ8Z3K2M9Y7V4X6B1N",
  "type": "subscription.renewed",
  "created_at": "2025-03-14T09:41:22Z",
  "data": {
    "subscription_id": "sub_9Xk2LmQ7pR4t",
    "customer_id": "cus_4Fh8Za1",
    "status": "active",
    "plan_id": "plan_growth_monthly",
    "quantity": 5,
    "period_start": "2025-03-14T09:41:22Z",
    "period_end": "2025-04-14T09:41:22Z",
    "amount_paid": 19600,
    "currency": "usd",
    "invoice_id": "in_1Q8xT2",
    "payment_id": "pay_7Kd3"
  }
}
```

> Trade-off: the minimal payload is cheaper to store and parse, but consumers must call your API to get full context. The full payload is self-contained and better for event-driven architectures.

## 4. Companion HTTP headers

```
POST /webhooks/billing
Content-Type: application/json
X-Webhook-Id: evt_01HQ8Z3K2M9Y7V4X6B1N
X-Webhook-Event: subscription.renewed
X-Webhook-Timestamp: 1741851682
X-Webhook-Signature: t=1741851682,v1=5257a869e7ecebeda32affa62cdca3fa51cad7e77a0e56ff536d0ce8e108d8bd
X-Webhook-Delivery-Attempt: 1
Idempotency-Key: evt_01HQ8Z3K2M9Y7V4X6B1N
```

`X-Webhook-Signature` is an HMAC-SHA256 of `"{timestamp}.{raw_body}"` using a shared secret — always verify against the **raw** body before JSON parsing, and reject timestamps older than ~5 minutes to prevent replay attacks.

## 5. Design notes

- **Distinguish renewal events.** Use `subscription.renewed` for a successful recurring charge, and separate types for `subscription.created`, `subscription.updated`, `subscription.canceled`, `invoice.payment_failed`. A renewal that fails to charge should emit `invoice.payment_failed`, not `subscription.renewed`.
- **Idempotency.** Consumers should store `id` (or `request.idempotency_key`) and make handlers idempotent — webhooks are delivered at-least-once and will be retried.
- **Versioning.** Bump `api_version` for breaking changes; add new optional fields freely within a version.
- **Ordering.** Don't rely on event order. Use `current_period_start` / `cycle_number` to detect gaps and re-sync.
- **Retries.** Exponential backoff over 24–72 hours (e.g., 8 attempts). `delivery_attempt` tells the consumer which try they're seeing.
- **PII.** Avoid embedding card numbers; `last4` only. Consider an option to fetch customer details via API instead of inlining them.
- **Amounts.** Always integers in the currency's minor unit (cents) to avoid floating-point errors; state the currency in ISO 4217 lowercase.
- **Timestamps.** ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z` suffix, millisecond precision.


## 2. Envelope fields

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Unique event ID (`evt_…`). **Idempotency key** — store it and ignore duplicates. |
| `type` | string | Event type. Use `subscription.renewed` (past tense = event already happened). |
| `version` | string | Schema version of *this payload*. Bump on breaking changes; add fields freely. |
| `created_at` | RFC 3339 | When the event was generated (not when delivered). |
| `livemode` | bool | `false` for test/sandbox events. |
| `data.object` | object | Full resource snapshot at renewal time. |
| `data.previous_attributes` | object | Only fields that changed — useful for diffing/audit. Optional. |
| `context` | object | Tenant/account scope, source system. |
| `request.idempotency_key` | string | Deterministic key for this renewal occurrence. |

## 3. Design decisions worth stating

**Snapshot, not a delta.** `data.object` contains the complete subscription state after renewal. Receivers rarely need to call back to fetch state, and a snapshot is replay-safe. `previous_attributes` is a convenience diff only.

**Money as integers + explicit currency.** All amounts are minor units (cents) as integers, with `currency` always present. Never floats.

**Timestamps are UTC RFC 3339.** `current_period_start` / `current_period_end` define the new billing period. `next_billing_date` can be derived from `current_period_end`; include it only if your engine can schedule differently (e.g. proration anchors).

**`billing_reason` distinguishes renewal from other causes.** Values like `subscription_create`, `subscription_cycle`, `subscription_update`, `subscription_cancel` — so consumers can distinguish a true renewal from a plan change.

**Payment details are embedded, not linked.** The invoice and payment method summary travel with the event so the consumer can reconcile without an extra API call. Don't include raw card numbers, CVVs, or full PAN — only `brand`/`last4`/expiry.

**`metadata` is passthrough.** This is the extension point for your own identifiers (workspace ID, seat count, etc.). Keep it small.

**`discount` is optional and nullable.** Include the applied promotion so consumers can display "20% off" without extra lookups.

## 4. Companion event types

Renewal is one of a family; keep the names consistent:

```
subscription.created
subscription.renewed
subscription.updated
subscription.trial_started
subscription.trial_ended
subscription.paused
subscription.resumed
subscription.canceled
subscription.expired
invoice.payment_failed
invoice.paid
```

## 5. Delivery contract

**Headers**

```
Content-Type: application/json
X-Webhook-Id: evt_01JZQ8M4K2P9F7T3X
X-Webhook-Timestamp: 1748781603
X-Webhook-Signature: t=1748781603,v1=5257a869e7ec...
```

**Signature** — HMAC-SHA256 over `"{timestamp}.{raw_body}"`, secret per endpoint. Verify with a constant-time comparison and reject timestamps older than 5 minutes (replay window). Always sign the **raw** body, before JSON parsing.

**Retries** — exponential backoff (e.g. 5s, 30s, 2m, 10m, 1h, 6h) for non-2xx or network failures. Treat any 2xx as success. The `id` stays the same across retries.

**Ordering is not guaranteed.** Consumers must be order-independent; use `current_period_end` or the event timestamp to detect out-of-order delivery.

**Respond fast.** Acknowledge with `2xx` within ~5 seconds and enqueue heavy processing. If you need the body, persist it first.

**Idempotency recipe** — insert `event.id` into a unique table inside the same transaction as your side effects; on conflict, return `200` and skip.

## 6. Minimal variant (if you need something leaner)

```json
{
  "id": "evt_01JZQ8M4K2P9F7T3X",
  "type": "subscription.renewed",
  "created_at": "2025-06-01T12:00:03Z",
  "data": {
    "subscription_id": "sub_1N9xK2mQ7rT4",
    "customer_id": "cus_8Kd3Lp0Z",
    "plan_id": "plan_pro_monthly",
    "quantity": 3,
    "amount_paid": 11760,
    "currency": "usd",
    "period_start": "2025-06-01T12:00:00Z",
    "period_end": "2025-07-01T12:00:00Z",
    "invoice_id": "in_7Rt2Wq9K",
    "metadata": { "workspace_id": "ws_2048" }
  }
}
```

Use this only if your consumers are simple; the full payload pays for itself the first time someone asks "what plan did they renew onto?"

runs.prompt: Design the JSON payload a webhook sends when a subscription is renewed.
runs.output:
# Subscription Renewal Webhook — Payload Design

## 1. Design principles

| Principle | Rationale |
|---|---|
| **Thin envelope + versioned event types** | Consumers subscribe to `subscription.renewed` and can ignore unknown fields; `api_version` lets you evolve the schema without breaking old consumers. |
| **Snapshot, not a delta** | The payload is the state *after* renewal, so consumers don't need to call back to fetch it. |
| **Immutable event identity** | `id` is stable across retries so the receiver can dedupe. |
| **Integer minor units** | Amounts as `1999` (cents), never floats. Currency as ISO 4217 (`"usd"`). |
| **UTC ISO-8601 timestamps** | Unambiguous, sortable. |
| **Minimal PII** | Only ship what the receiver needs to fulfill the event (e.g. email for a receipt). |
| **Extensible via `metadata`** | Merchant-specific data rides along without schema changes. |

---

## 2. Canonical payload

```json
{
  "id": "evt_1PzQ8mK2rT9yL4nB",
  "type": "subscription.renewed",
  "api_version": "2024-06-01",
  "created_at": "2024-06-01T12:00:03Z",
  "livemode": false,
  "account_id": "acct_9f3a2b",

  "data": {
    "object": {
      "id": "sub_1NqR7tK3wX",
      "object": "subscription",
      "status": "active",

      "customer": {
        "id": "cus_Qp2mL8vA",
        "email": "ada@example.com",
        "name": "Ada Lovelace"
      },

      "plan": {
        "id": "plan_pro_monthly",
        "name": "Pro (Monthly)",
        "amount": 4900,
        "currency": "usd",
        "interval": "month",
        "interval_count": 1
      },

      "quantity": 3,
      "discount": {
        "id": "di_55aBc",
        "percent_off": 20,
        "ends_at": "2024-09-01T00:00:00Z"
      },

      "current_period_start": "2024-06-01T12:00:00Z",
      "current_period_end": "2024-07-01T12:00:00Z",
      "billing_cycle_anchor": "2024-01-01T12:00:00Z",

      "trial_end": null,
      "cancel_at_period_end": false,
      "canceled_at": null,
      "ended_at": null,

      "payment": {
        "invoice_id": "in_1PzQ8mK",
        "payment_intent_id": "pi_3PzQ8mK2rT9y",
        "status": "succeeded",
        "amount": 11760,
        "amount_due": 11760,
        "amount_paid": 11760,
        "currency": "usd",
        "payment_method": {
          "id": "pm_1PzQ8m",
          "type": "card",
          "brand": "visa",
          "last4": "4242",
          "exp_month": 11,
          "exp_year": 2026
        },
        "attempted_at": "2024-06-01T12:00:02Z",
        "failure_code": null,
        "failure_message": null
      },

      "proration": null,
      "previous_period_end": "2024-06-01T12:00:00Z",

      "metadata": {
        "workspace_id": "ws_7781",
        "seats_purchased": "3"
      }
    }
  },

  "request": {
    "idempotency_key": "renewal_sub_1NqR7tK3wX_2024-06-01",
    "source": "billing_scheduler"
  }
}
```

---

## 3. Field reference

**Envelope**

- `id` — Unique event ID. **Same across all delivery attempts.** Use as the consumer's idempotency key.
- `type` — Dot-namespaced event type. See the event catalog below.
- `api_version` — Schema version of `data.object`. Bump on breaking changes; additive fields don't require a bump.
- `created_at` — When the event was *generated* (not when delivered).
- `livemode` — `false` for sandbox/test traffic. Always lets the consumer skip test events.
- `account_id` — Which merchant account the event belongs to (multi-tenant platforms).

**`data.object`** — The renewed subscription.

- `id` — Your subscription ID (the resource the event is about).
- `status` — Post-renewal status: `active`, `past_due`, `trialing`, `canceled`.
- `customer` — Denormalized snapshot; `id` is the source of truth, the rest is convenience.
- `plan` — The plan that was charged. Include `amount`/`currency`/`interval` so consumers can reconcile without a lookup.
- `quantity` — Number of units billed.
- `discount` — Applied promotion, if any (`percent_off` or `amount_off`).
- `current_period_start` / `current_period_end` — The new billing window. `previous_period_end` is the old one, so a consumer can compute the delta without a second call.
- `trial_end` — Non-null if this renewal *converted a trial to paid*. Useful for `trial_will_end` vs. `subscription.renewed` discrimination.
- `cancel_at_period_end` / `canceled_at` / `ended_at` — Lifecycle flags; `canceled_at` non-null means the renewal was a final one.
- `payment` — The money movement. `invoice_id` links to your billing system; `payment_intent_id` links to the PSP.
- `payment_method` — Tokenized reference + non-sensitive display fields only. **Never** include PAN, CVV, or full track data.
- `proration` — Non-null when the renewal included a mid-cycle adjustment (plan change, seat addition):
  ```json
  "proration": {
    "amount": 2450,
    "currency": "usd",
    "reason": "quantity_change",
    "period_start": "2024-06-01T12:00:00Z",
    "period_end": "2024-07-01T12:00:00Z"
  }
  ```
- `metadata` — Pass-through key/value pairs you set on the subscription.

---

## 4. Event catalog

Emit a family of events so consumers don't have to infer intent from a single generic one:

| Event type | When it fires | Key differentiator |
|---|---|---|
| `subscription.renewed` | Successful automatic renewal | `payment.status = "succeeded"` |
| `subscription.renewal_failed` | Charge failed; retry pending | `payment.failure_code` set, `status = "past_due"` |
| `subscription.trial_will_end` | 3 days before trial converts | `trial_end` in the future |
| `subscription.created` | New subscription (incl. trial) | `status = "trialing"` or `"active"` |
| `subscription.updated` | Plan/quantity change | `previous_attributes` present |
| `subscription.canceled` | End of term reached | `ended_at` set |
| `invoice.paid` | Any invoice settled (incl. one-off) | Not subscription-scoped |

For `subscription.updated`, add a diff block instead of only the snapshot:

```json
"previous_attributes": {
  "plan": { "id": "plan_pro_monthly" },
  "quantity": 3
}
```

---

## 5. Delivery contract (headers)

Put transport concerns in headers, not the body:

```http
POST /webhooks/billing
Content-Type: application/json
X-Webhook-Id: evt_1PzQ8mK2rT9yL4nB
X-Webhook-Timestamp: 1717243203
X-Webhook-Signature: t=1717243203,v1=5257a869e7ec...
X-Webhook-Delivery-Attempt: 1
```

- **Signature** — `HMAC-SHA256(secret, "{timestamp}.{raw_body}")`, hex-encoded. Always sign the *raw* bytes, before JSON parsing.
- **Timestamp** — Include in the signed string to prevent replay. Reject if the timestamp is more than ~5 minutes old.
- **Attempt** — Lets the consumer distinguish a retry from a duplicate event.
- **Delivery semantics** — At-least-once. Retries with exponential backoff (e.g. 5s → 30m, ~8 attempts over 72h). Non-2xx = failure. **Ordering is not guaranteed.**

---

## 6. Consumer checklist

1. **Verify signature first**, using the raw body and a constant-time comparison.
2. **Check the timestamp window** to block replays.
3. **Dedupe on `id`** — store it with a TTL longer than your retry window (≥ 7 days).
4. **Return 2xx quickly** — enqueue and process asynchronously; long processing causes timeouts and duplicate deliveries.
5. **Don't rely on ordering** — use `current_period_start`/`end` or the event `id` for sequencing.
6. **Treat `data.object` as read-only** — it's a point-in-time snapshot; a later `subscription.updated` may contradict it.
7. **Handle unknown `type` and unknown fields gracefully** — forward compatibility.
8. **Reconcile on `payment.invoice_id`** — the durable link back to your ledger.

---

## 7. Test payload (minimal, for local development)

```json
{
  "id": "evt_test_0001",
  "type": "subscription.renewed",
  "api_version": "2024-06-01",
  "created_at": "2024-06-01T12:00:03Z",
  "livemode": true,
  "account_id": "acct_test",
  "data": {
    "object": {
      "id": "sub_test_0001",
      "object": "subscription",
      "status": "active",
      "customer": { "id": "cus_test_0001", "email": "test@example.com", "name": "Test User" },
      "plan": { "id": "plan_test", "name": "Test Plan", "amount": 1000, "currency": "usd", "interval": "month", "interval_count": 1 },
      "quantity": 1,
      "current_period_start": "2024-06-01T12:00:00Z",
      "current_period_end": "2024-07-01T12:00:00Z",
      "payment": { "invoice_id": "in_test_0001", "status": "succeeded", "amount": 1000, "currency": "usd" },
      "metadata": {}
    }
  }
}
```

> Note: `livemode: true` above is intentional for the local test fixture — flip it to `false` if your sandbox convention is the opposite. Keep the field present either way so consumers can branch on it.

## Example `site.config.json`

```json
{
  "site": {
    "title": "Astro Handbook",
    "description": "Notes and tutorials on building static sites.",
    "baseUrl": "https://example.com/",
    "basePath": "/"
  },
  "build": {
    "outputDir": "public",
    "cleanOutput": true,
    "minify": true,
    "draft": false
  },
  "language": {
    "default": "en",
    "fallback": "en",
    "direction": "ltr",
    "locales": {
      "en": "English",
      "de": "Deutsch",
      "fr": "Français"
    }
  },
  "theme": {
    "name": "default",
    "stylesheet": "/assets/css/main.css"
  },
  "author": {
    "name": "Jane Doe",
    "email": "jane@example.com"
  }
}
```

## Field reference

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `site.title` | string | Title used in `<title>`, headers, RSS feeds, and sitemap metadata. |
| `site.baseUrl` | string | Absolute origin + path the site is served from (e.g. `https://example.com/`). Used to build absolute URLs for canonical tags, sitemaps, and Open Graph images. |
| `site.basePath` | string | Optional sub-path when the site is hosted under a prefix (e.g. `/blog/`). |
| `build.outputDir` | string | Directory (relative to project root) where generated files are written. |
| `build.cleanOutput` | boolean | Wipe the output directory before each build to remove stale files. |
| `build.minify` | boolean | Minify HTML/CSS/JS in production builds. |
| `build.draft` | boolean | Include pages marked as drafts. |
| `language.default` | string | BCP‑47 tag for the language used when no locale is specified (e.g. `en`). |
| `language.fallback` | string | Locale used when a translation for a page is missing. |
| `language.locales` | object | Map of supported locale codes to display names. |

## Minimal variant

If you only need the four requested options:

```json
{
  "title": "Astro Handbook",
  "baseUrl": "https://example.com/",
  "outputDir": "public",
  "defaultLanguage": "en"
}
```

## Notes

- **JSON has no comments.** If you want inline documentation, name the file `site.config.jsonc` and use `//` or `/* */` comments — most SSGs (Vite/Astro, Hugo, Eleventy with a JSON plugin) will parse it with a JSONC-tolerant loader.
- **Trailing slashes matter.** Keep `baseUrl` consistent with your deployment target: `https://example.com/` for a domain root, `https://example.com/docs/` for a sub-path.
- **Environment overrides.** A common pattern is to keep the committed config minimal and layer CI-specific values on top, e.g. `SITE_BASE_URL=https://staging.example.com/ npm run build`.
